verdicts.claim: By default SQLite auto-checkpoints when a COMMIT leaves the WAL at 1000 pages or more, and when the last connection closes
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "SQLite will automatically checkpoint whenever a COMMIT occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more in size, or when the last database connection on a database file closes."

verdicts.claim: the threshold is changeable via PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT
verdicts.evidence: wal.html says the threshold "can be changed or automatic checkpointing can be completely disabled" and names SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT; forum thread points to PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint.

verdicts.claim: Auto-checkpoints are PASSIVE: they copy as many frames as possible without waiting and never invoke the busy handler
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: checkpoints "by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE"; API doc: "The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode."

verdicts.claim: FULL waits (via busy handler) for writers to finish and readers to reach the latest snapshot; RESTART waits until readers no longer use the WAL; TRUNCATE truncates to zero bytes
verdicts.evidence: API doc: FULL blocks "until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot"; RESTART blocks "until all readers are reading from the database file only"; TRUNCATE "truncates the log file to zero bytes".

verdicts.claim: These modes block new writers but not new readers while waiting
verdicts.evidence: API doc (FULL): "This mode blocks new database writers while it is pending, but new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded." RESTART: "blocks new database writer attempts while it is pending, but does not impede readers".

verdicts.claim: A normal checkpoint does not shrink the WAL file; the file is rewound and overwritten from the start unless journal_size_limit is set or TRUNCATE
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file ... it merely causes SQLite to start overwriting the WAL file from the beginning" unless journal_size_limit pragma is set.

verdicts.claim: Operators under heavy load pair default auto-checkpoints with a separate maintenance task that checks WAL size and issues TRUNCATE checkpoints
verdicts.evidence: Guix message returned HTTP 502 on two fetches; wal.html only supports running periodic checkpoints in a separate thread, not size-checking + TRUNCATE.

verdicts.claim: The wal2 branch alternates between two WAL files so continuous writers no longer cause unbounded growth, but long-running readers can still prevent
verdicts.evidence: wal2.md: "In wal2 mode, wal files do not grow indefinitely even if the checkpointer never has a chance to finish uninterrupted"; brandur (2024-01-13): "juggling two wal files". Not-mainline and reader caveat only implied ("may only be accessed by versions of SQLite compiled from this branch"; checkpoint waits until readers' snapshots include the first file).

verdicts.claim: Checkpoint starvation: if at least one read transaction is always open, checkpoints never reach the end of the WAL and the WAL grows without bound
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: if "there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete" and "the WAL file will grow without bound."

verdicts.claim: A prepared statement that is stepped but never reset or finalized keeps its transaction open and is a common cause of a WAL that never shrinks
verdicts.evidence: drh: not invoking sqlite3_reset() "will likely be leaving some transactions open, which will prevent the checkpoint from happening and resetting the WAL file." The 'check file size' diagnostic step is not stated in either post.
